name: Beno
overview: Beno was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically associated with the Merarite clan, descendants of Merari, son of Levi. He is uniquely identified as the son of Jaaziah, situating him within the Levitical genealogies important for understanding priestly divisions and duties. His lineage connects him to the organized service of the tabernacle as outlined in the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Beno' is a proper name meaning 'son,' reflecting a common Hebrew naming practice but was not given directly by God. This name appears in 1 Chronicles 24:26, indicating his identity within the Levitical family structure without additional titular significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Beno as the son of Jaaziah, establishing his direct paternal relationship as noted in 1 Chronicles 24:27. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text for Beno.
scriptureSignificance: Beno's significance lies in his place within the Levitical order, specifically among the Merarites, who were entrusted with particular responsibilities related to the tabernacle's service. His identification as Jaaziah's son contributes to the detailed genealogical records that structured the priestly divisions, underscoring the biblical emphasis on orderly worship and service to God.
